name: Mohammad Imran Hossain
role: Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Fellow | Medical AI & Computational Oncology

paragraphs: MSCA doctoral researcher at Karolinska Institutet working at the intersection of medical imaging, artificial intelligence, and cancer epidemiology. My doctoral research investigates mammography-based breast cancer risk prediction and the predictive value of a negative breast MRI, with the aim of informing evidence-based, personalized screening strategies.

My research experience spans computational pathology, spatial transcriptomics, multimodal data analysis, and accelerated MRI reconstruction. Through research appointments in France and the Netherlands and an Erasmus Mundus education across three European countries, I have developed computational workflows that connect imaging and molecular data with clinically motivated questions. My methodological interests include self-supervised representation learning, multiple-instance learning, rigorous model evaluation, and trustworthy medical AI.

entries.title: MSCA Doctoral Fellow — Medical AI and Computational Oncology
bullets: Investigating AI-based breast cancer risk prediction and personalized screening within the HER-CARE MSCA Doctoral Network (DC09), in the Department of Medical Epidemiology and Biostatistics.
Developing and evaluating mammography-based approaches to short-term breast cancer risk prediction, connecting imaging information with subsequent cancer outcomes and epidemiological data.
Examining the predictive value of a negative breast MRI to help characterize future cancer risk and inform decisions about supplemental imaging and screening intervals.
Research priorities include calibration, consistency of performance across populations, and clinically meaningful evaluation of predicted risk.

pages.heading: Selected Machine Learning and Medical Imaging Projects

entries.title: Automatic Brain Tissue Segmentation from MRI
entries.meta: University of Girona | MAIA Segmentation Challenge | 2023
bullets: Developed pipelines for gray matter, white matter, and cerebrospinal fluid segmentation on IBSR18 brain MRI, incorporating N4 bias-field correction, anisotropic diffusion, normalization, patch extraction, and data augmentation.

Compared probabilistic atlas-based segmentation with U-Net, LinkNet, and 2D/3D nnU-Net. The 3D nnU-Net achieved a mean Dice score of 0.937 ± 0.012; the project placed second in the MAIA brain tissue segmentation challenge.

entries.title: Cardiac Structure Segmentation from 2D Echocardiograms
bullets: Developed and compared U-Net and nnU-Net pipelines for segmentation of the left ventricular endocardium, left ventricular epicardium, and left atrium in 2D echocardiography.
nnU-Net achieved Dice scores of 0.94, 0.91, and 0.93, respectively, outperforming U-Net. Reported boundary errors were approximately 8–9 mm for HD95 and 0.28–0.44 mm for mean absolute distance.

entries.title: Skin Lesion Classification with Machine Learning and Deep Learning
entries.meta: University of Girona | MAIA CADx Challenges | 2023
bullets: Developed binary and multiclass classification pipelines using handcrafted features, feature selection, and classifier ensembles; implemented deep learning transfer learning with ResNet/ResNeXt, DenseNet, EfficientNet, and Swin transformers.

Used normalization, geometric and color augmentation, and prediction-averaging ensembles. The conventional machine learning pipeline achieved binary test accuracy of 0.8590 and multiclass test Cohen’s kappa of 0.74.

Best recorded deep learning ensemble validation results were 0.9070 binary accuracy, 0.9693 multiclass accuracy, and 0.9448 multiclass Cohen’s kappa. These validation results are distinct from the conventional pipeline’s test results. Both approaches placed second in their respective MAIA CADx challenges.

entries.title: Deformable Lung CT Registration
bullets: Developed pipelines to align inspiratory and expiratory lung CT scans from four COPDgene cases, including intensity preprocessing and lung segmentation.

Compared affine and B-spline registration with Elastix/Transformix against VoxelMorph. Mean target registration error was 2.08 ± 2.26 mm for the intensity-based approach and 2.18 ± 2.74 mm for VoxelMorph; limited training data constrained the learning-based approach.

entries.title: Breast Cancer Molecular Subtype Classification from Multi-omics Data
bullets: Integrated DNA methylation, copy-number variation, mRNA, and miRNA data from TCGA-BRCA for molecular subtype classification.
Implemented exploratory data analysis, preprocessing, early data fusion, and feature selection, and compared six classifiers. XGBoost achieved the best balanced multiclass accuracy of 0.82.

entries.title: Mammographic Breast Mass Detection
entries.meta: University of Cassino and Southern Lazio | 2023
paragraphs: Developed an end-to-end mammographic mass detection pipeline combining multi-scale morphological shifting, mean shift filtering, k-means segmentation, feature extraction, and machine learning classification using the uCAS ML framework. Reported sensitivity was 0.96, specificity 0.95, and accuracy 0.95. Presented the work as a poster at the 17th EXCITE Summer School on Biomedical Imaging.

entries.title: Skin Lesion Classification with Transfer Learning and Hybrid Models
entries.meta: University of Cassino and Southern Lazio | 2023
paragraphs: Developed a two-stage classification pipeline on ISIC 2017 dermoscopic images: benign versus other lesions, followed by melanoma versus seborrheic keratosis. Compared fine-tuned CNNs with pretrained features and machine learning classifiers after resizing, normalization, and class balancing. On the 600-image test set, Xception features with Random Forest achieved balanced multiclass accuracy of 0.79, compared with 0.76 for the best transfer learning models.

entries.title: Alzheimer’s Disease Classification from Imaging and Gene-expression Features
entries.meta: University of Cassino and Southern Lazio | MAIA Statistical Learning Challenge | 2023
paragraphs: Built a pipeline for Alzheimer’s disease versus controls, Alzheimer’s disease versus mild cognitive impairment, and mild cognitive impairment versus controls. Applied collinearity and correlation filtering, LASSO, Boruta, and PCA, and compared classifiers using 10-fold cross-validation. QDA with Boruta or LASSO gave reported training-set AUCs of 0.963, 0.831, and 0.876 for the three tasks, respectively; these are training-set results rather than held-out test estimates.
